category_title: Secondary PRU students with low self-worth and mainstream avoidance
minimal_context: The tutor is asking the student to complete a GCSE practice paper in a mainstream classroom setting.
dialogue:
TUTOR: We need to complete this GCSE practice paper today. It is important to finish this so you can prepare for your exams.

STUDENT: I know you need GCSEs to get to go to a good college to get a career. But the school wanting that good reputation so choosing the normal kids... but then the people that are below that standard are like the outcasts...

TUTOR: Let's just focus on the questions in front of you right now.

STUDENT: If you can get through mainstream then [sighs] congratulations basically... You either deal with it or you don't... I had to back away, it was too much.

TUTOR: You need to keep working. I heard about the incident in the hallway earlier, and you need to show you can behave and finish this assignment.

STUDENT: She pushed me over so I punched her in the face! You're always blaming me. The school's corrupt... They got me excluded... The internal exclusion happened... I can't avoid it...

options.A: Implement relatively tight timelines for completing the GCSE practice papers and other assignments throughout the school term.
options.B: Ensure the student participates in all decision-making processes regarding their behavior, using Person-Centered Planning (PCP) principles.
options.C: Implement a minimal yet demanding curriculum centered on a single extensive GCSE practice paper to simulate postsecondary expectations.
options.D: Establish a gradual reintegration schedule, starting with one day at school per week and increasing each subsequent week.
